false_positives: Deepseek's initial PKGBUILD assessment incorrectly flagged HTML entities (&quot;, &apos;) as shell injection vectors. These are formatting artifacts from XML/HTML encoding, not executable shell syntax. The model's second look correctly identified this as a false positive.
learnings: Models can misinterpret HTML/XML entity encoding as shell syntax when reviewing files that have been serialized or displayed in HTML contexts. Audit tools should preprocess files to decode entities before analysis, or train models to recognize encoding artifacts.

Tool errors (API failures, parsing errors) should not block a verdict when other critical files have been successfully audited and found safe. The audit framework should distinguish between 'inconclusive due to security uncertainty' and 'inconclusive due to tool failure'.
The 'second look' mechanism successfully caught and corrected a false positive, demonstrating the value of iterative review for ambiguous findings.
